City of Belvidere corporate limits (scripts/build_place_outline.py) — the ONLY municipal outline this instance ships, and it exists to carve one hole in a county source rather than to draw a city. Boone's Fire_Districts layer tiles every acre of the county, so a Belvidere address returned Fire District 2 while the Clerk's own district-rates report gives 18 of 55 tax codes no fire line at all — those 18 being the city's, which runs a MUNICIPAL fire department. TWENTY-TWO of its twenty-four rings are HOLES, unincorporated pockets the city annexed around, and they are load-bearing: a resident of one is not in the city, so they ARE in the fire district and keep their card. The even-odd test both the builder and pointInGeometry use gets that right, and the builder gates its own area against the Census's published AREALAND so a hole counted as solid (43.05 km² against a real 35.19) fails the build.

Bond County outline — gap-location geometry only. Bond is served as a judicial-circuit secondary with no dispatch entry, so this ships purely so its 2026-08-08 board gap record attaches to ground the gaps panel can locate.
Boone County coverage outline (scripts/build_county_outline.py) — gates the county's dispatch entries.

Boone's 3 library districts, pre-built by scripts/build_parcel_fabric_districts.py. Boone publishes NO library boundary — measured across its whole ArcGIS server (12 folders, 99 services) and its AGOL org (510 items) — so each district is the DISSOLVE of the parcels the county's own fabric assigns to the tax codes its Clerk's 2025 Taxcode Value within District Report puts in LYBV (18), LYCV (2) and LYNS (4), road voids closed at 75 ft by the same rules as the Rock Island files. Two of the three are seated in Winnebago and reach across the line; only their Boone slice is drawn. Bounds are an EQUALITY: the county levies exactly these three, and shipping only Ida would tell a Loves Park or Cherry Valley resident they are in no library district.

The cut is therefore unmoved and the boundaryNote is unretired; it now names the published descriptions instead of an outstanding ask. TWO MORE ARTIFACTS AT THAT CUT WERE FIXED 2026-08-10, both drawing as a line standing inside District 10 and each with its own cause. A 9 m wide, 408 m tall slice of Shiloh 4 fell east of the TIGER meridian but SOUTH OF BROADWAY, where the county's own description says there is no Shiloh 4 east of 34th Street at all (that ground is Shiloh 3) — District 11 territory standing inside District 10, now returned to the west side by testing each stranded part against Shiloh 3's own northern edge. And a 7 m wide, 190 m deep slot between Shiloh 3 and Shiloh 4, both walls District 10, which resolve_tiling's reach rule declined because the slot's mouth opens onto the District 5 township line and that rule is blind to shape; pass 2b adds the shape test, giving a crack to the district holding 90% of its outline. Inter-district cracks in this county score 50-58% and surrounded ones 87% or more, so the threshold is nowhere near anything. District 10 finished at 14 vertices, from 129. AND ROUND FOUR: four clicks near district borders answered that the point was not inside any district in this layer, all four in inter-district hairlines the reach rule leaves unowned by design. 0.0235% of the county, one click in four thousand, and a false answer every time — the point IS in a district, the county's file merely has a crack there, which is the same sentence that justifies closing these one layer down. Closed at both layers now (close_reopened() in the precinct builder, pass 2b here): a crack goes whole to the district holding most of its outline, or is split at 40 m per side when it is one of the two lattices spanning 9 and 14 km. Both files tile 100.0000% of Jefferson. THE DISSOLVE IS ALSO REPAIRED, from 2026-08-10, after a reader reported strange artifacts in these boundaries: they were real. A plain union of the precincts left 108 SLIVER HOLES (the worst 7,545 m long and 124 m wide, inside District 8; District 7 had 64 along one township line), and a hole is stroked, so each drew a dark line across a filled district. It also left five spurious parts — Districts 5 and 7 rendered as two disconnected blocks each because a crack ran the full width between two of their own precincts — and 28 overlapping pairs, worst 33,126 m2, pooled from the county's own overlapping precincts. The cause is upstream: build_jefferson_precincts.py simplifies each precinct independently AFTER repairing the county's cracks, and Douglas-Peucker is deterministic only on identical input, so shared edges diverge. That file is deliberately NOT re-cut — its residue is measured, asserted, byte-stable and now checked against the county's published descriptions — so resolve_tiling() repairs the dissolve instead: double-claimed ground to the lower-numbered district, unowned cracks to the district that is the only one within 150 m, then enclosed rings filled and sub-5,000 m2 dust dropped, every step with a ceiling asserted. Result is 13 districts, 13 parts, 0 sliver holes, worst overlap 74 m2 (rounding), tiling 99.988% of the county. Jefferson is the only dissolve in the fleet that needs this; every other county-board file built this way has holes of at most 191 m2, because their precincts arrived edge-matched.

Each crack is given to the precinct whose boundary is nearest (Voronoi over densified boundaries), then simplified to undo the vertex explosion that assignment causes — 99.949% coverage, median boundary shift 34 m, worst 153 m, all asserted. close_reopened() then gives the cracks that simplification reopens back to the precinct around them, so the shipped file tiles 100.0000% rather than 99.949%. THE TOLERANCE WAS 10 m UNTIL 2026-08-10 AND WAS ON THE WRONG SIDE OF A CLIFF: 10 m cannot remove a zig-zag whose amplitude is the 30 m Voronoi sampling step, so all 3,057 zig-zag vertices survived — invisible here, because a hairline between two precincts draws as nothing, and glaring in the board districts these dissolve into, where a reader reported them. 15 m leaves 31 of them for the same median shift and the same worst shift at a sixth of the vertices; an explicit despike() pass then removes the isolated spikes simplification keeps by construction (a vertex far off the chord between its neighbours WHEN they are close together, which is what separates a spike from a real corner) — 50 vertices, 0.008% of the county — including one 33 m south of a straight township line, on ground the county's raw file never drew. The county's own small Dodds 1 / Dodds 2 OVERLAP is deliberately left alone: a crack has no owner and can be assigned, two claims on the same ground cannot. SINCE 2026-08-10 THE SHAPES ARE CHECKED AGAINST A PUBLISHED SOURCE: Clerk Davis pointed at the county's precinct LEGAL DESCRIPTIONS page, which says in words where each precinct is, and check_legal_descriptions() asserts all 33 land in the congressional township their description declares (the grid quartered off the county outline, not off the precincts, so a swap among the whole-township ones cannot redefine the grid and pass), that 28 side-of-a-named-line claims hold, and that the three described section splits divide their township in the published proportion. Jackson County's 7 County Board districts, each electing TWO members (14 seats), and the FIRST in the fleet whose districts SPLIT precincts and are built anyway. Fifty-three of the county's 56 precincts take their district from its certified 5 November 2024 General canvass, which lists for each district's contest exactly the precincts that voted in it. THREE ARE REPORTED TWICE, under two districts each with their registration divided — Carbondale 21 (D6 600 / D7 282), Carbondale 24 (D5 609 / D6 98) and Murphysboro 4 (D3 166 / D5 391) — which is the county stating that a district line runs through them, and is why this county was recorded measured-shut beside Bureau, Cumberland, Douglas, Ford, Knox and Piatt. What that record missed is that it named the answer itself: the county publishes its adopted Board District Map as a VECTOR PDF whose seven districts are seven FILLED PATHS in the content stream — polygon objects with exact fill colours pairing one-for-one with the legend in legend order, not pixels to be classified (the method section warns against colour-sampling a RASTERISED map, and this is the opposite of that). The map is georeferenced to EPSG:3436 (Illinois State Plane West), established by fitting the union of the seven districts against TIGER's county boundary across candidate CRSs — 3436 matched the aspect ratio to four decimals and no other candidate did — and refined against the 53 unambiguous precincts; mean boundary offset 5.3 m, with the map's own scale bar independently confirming the scale. NOTHING TRACED SHIPS: the boundary is census geometry throughout, voting districts for the 53 whole precincts and whole census BLOCKS inside the three split ones, and the map is only ever allowed to choose between the two districts the canvass already names. FOUR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATIONS: all 53 unambiguous precincts land in the district the canvass names (53/53, at 98.3-100% of area); all three split precincts split between exactly the two it names (3/3); populations run 7,371-7,933 against a 7,568 ideal, worst deviation 4.83%, which a mis-assigned split precinct would destroy; and Murphysboro 4's census population divides 30.2/69.8 where its registration divides 29.8/70.2. THAT LAST CHECK IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED FOR THE OTHER TWO — Carbondale 21 and 24 hold SIU dormitories and student apartments, one block carrying 700 people in FOUR housing units, so census population does not predict registration there in either direction. Inside the three split precincts only FIVE blocks holding SIXTEEN people are less than 95% resolved by the georeferencing (scripts/build_jackson_boundaries.py; --check is the drift gate).

READ THE DOMAIN: the roster is on edgarcountyillinois.COM; the county's .GOV links across to it and does not carry the board. THIS ROSTER IS THE PAGE AND NOT THE RETURNS, and Edgar is the fleet's clearest case for that split — its 2022 and 2024 canvasses elected Phillip Ludington in District 6, the page names Samantha McCarty, and the Clerk's 2026 primary confirms her with a '2-year unexpired term' contest for the seat. A mid-term appointment is exactly what a completed canvass cannot show. Franklin County Board members keyed by district (3 districts seating 3 each, staggered — 9 members; 8/9 with a phone, 1 e-mail, and the role the county prints beside 5 of them). Scraped weekly from the county's own members page. THE PAGE IS A GRID AND IS READ AS ONE: its WP Table Builder cells carry data-y-index/data-x-index, and a flattened text read pairs every role with the WRONG member because column 0's role arrives before its own row's name — the Cumberland trap. Its Address column is every member's HOME address and is never read (the Madison/Peoria rule), asserted address-free in both stages. Its e-mail column is Cloudflare-obfuscated, the exact failure that silently emptied Brown County's seven addresses, so the scraper decodes data-cfemail and FAILS if the markup is present and nothing decodes. The 'Home or E-Mail' column ships only its e-mail half — a home telephone is the one contact this project does not publish and the county does not say which a cell holds. NO PARTY: the page publishes none, and taking it from the canvasses would label only the third of the board last on the ballot. THE CHAIR IS THE COUNTY'S OWN LABEL, not an inference from returns — the table names committee chairs by their committee and the board's own officers plainly ('Chairman', 'Vice Chairman'). The same run re-checks the district composition against the Clerk's results system and fails on a re-precincting or a redistricting.

Macon County Board members keyed by district (5 districts electing THREE members each, 15 seats; 15/15 with party and a county e-mail, 14 with a phone, 13 with a term-expiry date) — scraped weekly from the county's own board-members page, which is the ONLY place Macon publishes which district a member sits for. Party and district arrive as one token ("D-1", "R-4"). PHONES SHIP AS SEVEN DIGITS, as the county publishes them: Macon is entirely area code 217, but a member's mobile can be from anywhere and prefixing would reach a stranger rather than fail visibly — the county's own home/cell labels are kept instead. THE DOMAIN IS maconcounty.illinois.gov; maconcountyil.gov has no DNS record at all and shipped as a dead card link from 2026-08-04 until this change.

Menard County commissioners keyed by district (5 SINGLE-member districts; 5/5 with a phone and a county e-mail, plus the year each was elected or appointed) — scraped weekly from the county's own board page. DISTRICT 1'S E-MAIL LINK AND ITS LABEL DISAGREE — the page links djwhitley@ and displays dwhitley@ — and the HREF ships, because that is where the county's own page actually sends mail; the run prints a NOTE rather than resolving it silently. Henry's precinct -> polling place table, all 52 precincts. THE SOURCE IS THE CLERK'S OWN POLLING PLACES DIRECTORY, and finding it is the point: the county GIS office sent the precinct shapefile on 2026-08-06 with no polling assignment and said plainly that a polling list is the Clerk's record, not theirs, so this sat open for five days. Clerk Barbara Link answered on 2026-08-11 with one sentence — "I have pdf precinct maps on my webpage ... Also, I have polling place locations as well" — which reads as a brush-off and is a POINTER, and the pointer was correct: her directory lists all 52 locations, one per precinct, and had been reachable for the entire life of this project without anyone opening it. The Stephenson lesson, a second time. THE JOIN IS ON THE PRECINCT'S OWN FIELD, not the listing title, because the title is not a key: the county writes "Colona 3- Colona Activity Center" without the space and "Andover Village Hall" with no precinct prefix at all. ONE ALIAS, ENUMERATED: sixteen townships hold a single precinct and the two sources disagree about its number ("Alba" in the directory, "Alba 1" in the shapefile), so a bare name maps to "<name> 1" ONLY where the shapefile has exactly one precinct in that township and no bare form; anything else fails the build. scripts/build_henry_precinct_polling.py refuses to write unless the directory's own stated listing count parses and all 52 precincts resolve — a partial join would leave a resident with a blank row on the one card where being wrong sends them to the wrong building. REFRESHED WEEKLY by .github/workflows/update-henry-precinct-polling.yml (Fri 18:00 UTC), the fleet's first scheduled polling job — the other three are operator steps, and this field is the one where staleness sends someone to the wrong building. The job opens a PR only when a polling place actually moved, not when the fetch date did.

Montgomery's precinct -> polling place table, all 38 precincts across 24 buildings (12 precincts share a site with another). THE SOURCE IS THE CLERK'S PUBLISHED LIST, NOT THE GIS LAYER THAT ARRIVED WITH IT. A polling place is the one field on this card where being stale sends a resident to the wrong building on election day, so the election authority's list wins. scripts/build_montgomery_precinct_polling.py keeps the GIS layer as a self-retiring cross-check: it names those disagreements and FAILS if the layer's answer changes, so a county refresh that fixes them is noticed rather than hidden.

Montgomery County Board members keyed by district (7 districts electing TWO members each; 14/14 with a direct phone AND a county e-mail, four with a second published number) — scraped weekly from the county's own board page. The page rather than the Clerk's members PDF: checked 2026-08-06 the PDF still named two members who had been replaced, so the two county documents are trusted for different things — the PDF for district COMPOSITION, the page for names. The Board Chairman is badged on his own district row; he holds a district seat, so there is no countywide section. Peoria County Board members keyed by district (18 SINGLE-member districts — the app's largest single-member board; 18/18 with party and e-mail, 12 with phone). The Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson are badged on their own district rows — both hold district seats — and only where the county's index page states the role.

Tazewell County Board members keyed by district (3 districts seating 21 members) plus a `chair` key for the COUNTYWIDE-elected Board Chairman (the McHenry shape). The scraper records the one district assignment the county's two surfaces disagree about instead of silently picking the tidier arithmetic.

Iroquois County Board members keyed by district (4 districts, four members each; 16/16 with phone, 15 with e-mail, every seat with a home town and term-expiry year). Scraped weekly from the county's own table, which prints ROMAN numerals the scraper converts to the integers its GIS keys by. Chairman and Vice Chairman are badged on their own district rows — both hold district seats.

At-large county boards, keyed like il-county-clerks.json. Counties that elect their board COUNTYWIDE have no district geometry, so their members ride the COUNTY card rather than a county-board dispatch entry (EXPANSION_GUIDE §1.5). Nineteen counties, 100 members, from THREE kinds of source. Scraped from a county page: Monroe, Randolph and MORGAN (commission form, 3 each), MASSAC 3, Pike 9, MOULTRIE 9, Brown 7, Schuyler 7, GREENE 7, SALINE 13, Calhoun 5, Putnam 5, Hamilton 5, GALLATIN 5 and ALEXANDER 2. Carried from a document because the county has no readable website: EDWARDS 3 and WABASH 3. Read from certified returns because the county site is behind a captcha: UNION 5 and WILLIAMSON 3 (RETURNS_ROSTERS; each row names the election that seated it, since a canvass cannot show a mid-term appointment). ALEXANDER, added 2026-08-23, is the one county here whose board is BIGGER than its roster — three seats, two published, nobody naming the third — so its block carries `seats` beside its members and the County card prints the shortfall in the same words the districted counties use. It is also the reason MIN_MEMBERS stopped applying to counties that have an EXPECT_MEMBERS row: an exact count is a better guard than a range, and the range would have rejected a correct two-member read. Read the count from the builder's EXPECT_MEMBERS table, never from this sentence. Greene, added 2026-08-08, is the first of these that was ALREADY SERVED before its board arrived (a 7th-Circuit subcircuit answered there), so it moved tier without changing the coverage ring or any anchor. Edwards has no website at all (its Clerk said so on 2026-08-06, and the domain answers NOERROR with no A record), so its three commissioners come from a document she sent. Wabash, added 2026-08-17, is the second such county — wabashcounty.illinois.gov carries mail and serves no web page (port 80 answers 503, measured 5 Aug and re-checked 9 Aug) — and its three come from Clerk Will's e-mail of 2026-08-16; her e-mail lists only HOME addresses, which do not ship, so each Wabash row is a name alone, and nobody is marked Chairman until she answers which of the three chairs. The scraper carries both counties in DOCUMENT_ROSTERS and prints a NOT RE-READ line naming each document and its age on every run, because a weekly job that refreshes a hand-carried roster refreshes nothing. Each shipped county carries EITHER a sourceUrl or a sourceDocument+verified pair; the builder fails on a county with neither. MORGAN, added 2026-08-08, is the cautionary one: the county has TWO sites and this project read the wrong one for a day — morgancounty-il.GOV is a content-free React shell, while morgancounty-il.COM publishes all three with role, party, term dates and a personal e-mail apiece. GALLATIN, added 2026-08-21, is the only one of the nineteen that also carries a dispatch entry of its own for precincts alone, and the only one whose site had to be repaired to be read at all: gallatinco.illinois.gov omits its TLS intermediate, so the scraper chases the issuer the certificate itself names and pins its hash (AIA_INTERMEDIATES) rather than disabling verification. Its board page publishes a phone for two of the five and an e-mail for none, and nothing is invented for the other three.

De Witt County Board members keyed by district LETTER (A-D, three members each; 12/12 with e-mail, 10 with phone, committees per member). Washington County Board members keyed by district (3 districts, five members each; 15/15 with BOTH phone and e-mail). Cass County Board members keyed by district (4 districts seating 11 as 3/3/3/2; 11/11 phones, 8 e-mails, the Chairman badged on his own district row). Scraped weekly. Marshall County Board members keyed by district (3 districts, four members each; 12/12 phones, 11 e-mails, Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson badged, staggered 2026/2028 term years). Scraped weekly from the roster PDF, and the same scrape re-reads the township composition printed in that PDF's district headings and FAILS if it no longer matches the compiled boundary. Member home addresses are printed in that table and are deliberately never collected (the Madison precedent).

McDonough County Board members keyed by district (3 districts of SEVEN members each = 21, the county's full board), scraped weekly from http://mcg.mcdonough.il.us/members.html — the same page whose district headings supply the boundary composition, so membership and boundary move together and are checked together. The page prints every member's HOME ADDRESS and none is collected: the scraper reads only the phone out of that cell, and the builder refuses to write any field whose name looks like an address.

Fulton County Board members keyed by district (3 districts of FIVE members each = 15, the count the county states on the same page it publishes them). Scraped weekly from https://fultoncountyil.gov/county-board/members/, which publishes the board TWICE — a photo grid grouped by district (the only place the district is stated) and hidden popup blocks carrying the e-mail the grid omits — so the scraper joins the two halves on the member's name. Above District #1 sits a fourth section headed "Fulton County Board Chairman" containing a member who ALSO appears in his own district; it is read as the source of the Chair ROLE, not as a sixteenth seat, and the per-district ceiling fails the build if it is ever swept in as one. Stark County Board members keyed by district (2 districts of four = 8, the county's full board; 8/8 with an e-mail and a term year, Chair and Vice-Chair badged). Mason County Board members keyed by district (2 districts, four members each; 8/8 with party, phone, e-mail and a term year, Chairman and Vice-Chairman badged). Shelby County Board members keyed by district (11 districts electing TWO members each = 22 seats; currently 20 filled + District 7's two shipped AS VACANCIES exactly as the county prints them, 'Currently Vacant' with the seat's e-mail — dropping them would misstate the board's size). Scraped weekly from coboard.aspx and CROSS-CHECKED against the county's second published roster, the contacts.aspx e-mail directory: every directory row must match a card seat by e-mail and name, so a half-updated site fails instead of shipping whichever page the scraper read. Every filled seat carries party, a term string as printed ('2024–2028', 'through 2026') and an e-mail; 20/20 with a phone. The Chair and Vice Chair hold District 3's two seats, badged on their own rows with the role alias e-mail (shcoboardchair@/shcovicechair@) the county publishes beside each district address. White County Board members keyed by district (5 single-member districts) plus a top-level 'board' entry carrying the board's ONE published contact — the Clerk's e-mail and the PO Box the county prints for all five members (one address for five members is the board's, not five members', the Calhoun switchboard rule). Scraped weekly from the county's own board page, which lists name, party and Chair/Vice roles and NO districts: each member's district is joined from the certified-canvass table in build_white_county_board.py (2022 General elected all five by district; 2024 re-elected districts 3-4), matched surname + first initial and required UNIQUE. Any page name that table cannot place FAILS the weekly build instead of shipping a guess — a new member's district is a fact only a new certified document (or the Clerk) can supply.

White County's polling places keyed by shipped precinct name — the County Clerk's own POLLING PLACES list on her Elections page, eleven buildings covering all 18 precincts (Carmi's seven vote at one building; the builder refuses to write on any coverage short of 18/18). The page's 'Gray #24' is normalised to the GREY 24 spelling the county's own map, the census and the canvasses share, recorded in the builder. Coles County Board members keyed by district (12 single-member districts) plus a top-level 'board' entry carrying the County Board office's own address and phone — one office for twelve members is the board's, not each member's (the Calhoun switchboard rule), and it is the BOARD's rather than a county switchboard by measurement: the same navbar block reads Room 124 / (217) 348-0511 on the Treasurer's page and 701 7th St / (217) 348-0585 on the Sheriff's. Scraped weekly from the county's own board page. THE COUNTY'S BOARD-DISTRICT GIS LAYER ALSO CARRIES A MEMBER COLUMN AND IT IS NOT USED: that table is a 2022-04-23 snapshot which names six members who have since left the board, still reads term '2022' for District 11, and carries 2010 populations — so the app reads geometry from the service and people from here (scripts/coles_county_board_scraper.py has the six-name diff). No party, term or chair ships because the page publishes none; home addresses are printed under most members and are never parsed (the scraper keys on the contact row's ICON, not its href, because the address anchor is itself a tel: link). The county's committees page is the cross-check and a disagreement in either direction fails the weekly run.

Jo Daviess County Board members keyed by district (17 single-member districts — the seat count the boundary module exports, so the roster and the purchased geometry cannot drift apart silently). Scraped weekly from the county's own board page at jodaviesscountyil.gov (NEVER the old jodaviess.org, which answers every URL with its home page): name, party and term on every seat, Chair/Vice-Chair badged, plus a direct phone and an e-mail per member from each member's own directory page — 16 distinct numbers at first ship, so no switchboard hoist, and personal gmail/icloud addresses carried exactly as published. A seat the county prints as VACANT ships as a counted, never named vacancy (District 16 at first ship, the Livingston posture). The directory pages also print members' HOME ADDRESSES, which the scraper never parses (the Madison/Peoria precedent). The count guard counts SEATS (named + vacant = exactly 17, districts 1..17 each once), so a vacancy is distinguishable from a parse regression — and a changed district count reads as a reapportionment, which would need the purchased boundary re-licensed. PLUS A TOP-LEVEL 'board' ENTRY (2026-09-04) carrying WHERE THE BOARD MEETS rather than an office: the county's words are "County Board room, Third Floor, Jo Daviess County Courthouse", and the card's label reads "Board meets at" for that reason. A meeting room is not an office, and this is precisely the county whose per-member pages print the HOME addresses noted above — so the distinction is drawn in the label rather than blurred. min_keys is 17+1.

Cicero Public Library's seven elected trustees + the library's own contact, keyed by the Cook Clerk's tax AGENCY id (20060001, the fund tiling's own key) — the one Cook library body whose board the county publishes, filed in the Clerk's directory beside the Town of Cicero's government (build_cicero_library_trustees.py). Joined onto the library-district layer's Cook card; every other Cook agency stays name-only because no officeholder source exists for it.

Township governing bodies keyed by Census county-subdivision GEOID — supervisor (or Cicero's president), four trustees, clerk/assessor/collector/highway commissioner, township-hall contact — from the Cook County Clerk's directory TWNSP type (build_township_officials.py, 29 townships live; Evanston Township dissolved 2014 and is skipped by name). Party committeepersons and per-person contact never ship: the committeeperson records are the feed's one personal-e-mail surface, and the hall mailbox is shared township-wide. Townships in uncovered counties keep the identity-only card.

Hancock County Board members keyed by district (5 districts seating 15, three each, with a party letter per member). Scraped weekly from the county's board page, which publishes a name and a party and NOTHING ELSE — no e-mail, no phone, no term, and no chairman is named, so no row is badged one and there is no contact floor to set. THE COUNT IS THE GUARD for exactly that reason: with no field to watch, a page reshape shows up as a wrong number of members. Two parser traps are handled by construction. The page's <meta name="description"> REPEATS District One's three members verbatim, so anchoring on the first 'District One' in the document parses the meta tag and ships three members as a whole board; the body is found by scanning for the last occurrence. And the last district has no following <h2> to bound it — an unbounded region runs to the end of the document and swallows the site's footer navigation, which parsed District Five as 35 'members', most of them menu links. Each district is bounded to its own first <ul> instead, and a per-district ceiling fails the run loudly if that ever stops holding.

Richland County Board members keyed by district (7 single-member districts = 7 seats). Scraped weekly from the county's own board page, which publishes each member as a card carrying a name, a district line and a county e-mail — 7/7 carry one — and badges the Chairman. No party, term or phone ships because the page publishes none. THE PARSER IS SCOPED TO THE ROSTER BLOCK ON PURPOSE: the same page carries a committees section above it whose 'Chair:' and 'Members:' lines name people who do not sit on the board at all — five community members on the 708 Mental Health Committee alone — so a greedy read would ship a fourteen-name board for a seven-seat county. THE SAME WEEKLY RUN IS THE REDISTRICTING TRIPWIRE: it re-reads the county's own GIS board-district and voting-precinct layers and fails if either stops matching the shipped dissolve, which is this county's only automatic warning that its lines moved. What that check can and cannot see is stated in the builder: it verifies the county still publishes SEVEN districts over the same TWENTY-ONE precinct names, and does not re-run the spatial overlay, which needs the census fabric and does not belong in a weekly roster job.

Jackson County Board members keyed by district (7 districts electing TWO members each = 14 seats). Scraped weekly from the county's own board page, which groups members under 'District N Board Members' headings, plus each member's staff-directory entry for the county e-mail address — 14/14 carry one. THE HEADING IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THE DISTRICT, and that is this county's trap: a member's job title is their DISTRICT for twelve of the fourteen and their OFFICE for the other two, so the Chair's and Vice Chair's cards name no district at all and a parser keying on the title drops the two most prominent members and reports twelve seats for a fourteen-seat board. The directory entry states the district a second time, and the builder FAILS the run when the two county surfaces disagree rather than picking a winner. No party, phone or address ships because the county publishes none per member, and neither does the term length: the directory prints '2 Year Term' and '4 Year Term' but never a start or end date, and a term that cannot be placed in time tells a reader nothing. An eighth key, `board`, carries what the county publishes at the BOARD level rather than per member: a contact block headed 'County Board' with a Physical Address, the board's phone and its office hours, plus the second-floor Courtroom 4 where the page says the board MEETS — shipped as two separate rows, because an office and a meeting room are different places and one address must not stand for both.

Douglas County Board members keyed by district (7 single-member districts = 7 seats). THE COUNTY PUBLISHES NO BOARD MEMBERS PAGE AT ALL — no member list, no district pages, nothing in its navigation — so the roster is assembled weekly from the two county documents that each answer half of it, found through the WordPress backend behind its Next.js site rather than hardcoded: the annual COUNTY YEARBOOK names the seven people and gives each a county e-mail, and the certified ELECTION SUMMARY REPORTS say which numbered district each of them won, in the county's own numbering. THE YEARBOOK'S OWN NUMBERS ARE NOT DISTRICT NUMBERS and that is this county's trap: it lists members '1. Tom Hettinger', '2. Bibby Appleby', which reads exactly like a district column, while the certified returns put Hettinger in District 3 and Appleby in District 2 — taking list position as district would misplace SIX of the seven. Its per-member precinct lists cannot recover the district either; they contain at least one error, naming 'Camargo 1 & 2' for a member whose district holds Camargo 2 and 3. So the join is on SURNAME and the builder FAILS when the two documents stop naming the same seven people. Each row carries the election that seated the member, because a certified return names who WON rather than who holds the seat today (the Scott reasoning) and the yearbook is what corroborates that they still do. SIX OF SEVEN E-MAILS SHIP: the yearbook prints District 1's address on the domain 'douglascountuil.gov', a typo for the 'douglascountyil.gov' the other six use, and a domain check drops it rather than shipping a dead address or silently correcting a character in someone's contact detail. HOME ADDRESSES NEVER SHIP, and the yearbook prints one for every member. The term line does not ship either: it reads 'November 2024' / 'November 2026' with nothing saying whether that is the seating election or the term's end, and both readings contradict the returns for at least one member.

Vermilion County Board members keyed by district (9 districts x 3 members = 27 seats). PEOPLE COME FROM THE COUNTY'S OWN MEMBERS PAGE, reached by supplying the intermediate certificate the county's server omits — chased from the AIA URI the county's own leaf certificate names, pinned by SHA-256, and NEVER by disabling verification. NOT from the county's district layer, whose attribute table carries three Name/Party/Elected/Email sets per district and is a 2018 snapshot on a retired e-mail domain: the Coles rule holds, an attribute table on a boundary layer is a snapshot of whenever that layer was published. FOUR TRAPS IN ONE TABLE, each handled rather than absorbed: ONE NAME IS INVERTED (twenty-six rows read "First Last" and one reads "Auter, Tara"), so the comma form is flipped and the flip is PRINTED on every run rather than becoming a silent edit to somebody's name; ROLES RIDE THE NAME CELL ("Steve Miller (Chairman)"), split to their own field because leaving them in ships a name nobody is called; ONE E-MAIL CELL CARRIES A PHONE TOO, so the cell is tokenised rather than taken whole; and SURNAMES ARE NOT KEYS, because District 4 seats two McFaddens. The board office's own address and phone ride each district's roster block, so a card for a member with no direct line still says where to reach the board. The county's own "Elected/Appointed" year ships as "on the board since", labelled that way because the county does not say which of the two it was. The board LANDING page's staff table is never read for members: it lists the HR director and the office manager alongside the chairman.

Wayne County Board members keyed by district (7 districts x 2 members = 14 seats). Scraped weekly from the county's own board page — the SAME page the district composition was read from, so re-scraping it every week is this county's redistricting tripwire (the builder fails if a district's re-read precinct list stops matching the shipped composition; District 7 is checked as the known subset, since the page has never named Fairfield 1 or Fairfield 2). Each district's paragraph names two members with an optional Chairman or Vice Chairman title — Daryl Hargrave (D1) and Gene Kollak (D7) hold the two titles the page states. No e-mail, phone, party or term is published, so none ships.

Clay County Board members keyed by district LETTER (A-N, one member each = 14 seats; 14/14 with a phone, as the county prints it, dots and all). Scraped weekly from the county's own MEMBERS page — an Elementor team widget per member, the county's maintained list (the Alexander rule), each position line stating the district ('County Board - District K'; the Chair's card carries the office in the same line: 'County Board Chair - District C'). Each card prints its phone TWICE (an image-overlay copy and a content copy) and the scraper requires the two to agree. ROLES COME FROM TWO COUNTY SURFACES THAT MUST AGREE: the Chair is marked on his own card AND named in the county-board page's Chairman tab, and the build fails if they name different people. The VICE CHAIRMAN is named only in that prose, under a different form of her name — the board page writes 'Barbara McGrew', the members page prints 'Barb Mcgrew' — so the role joins by surname, required unique, with the join PRINTED on every run; the shipped name is the members page's exactly as printed, lowercase g included (the Fulton 'Karl WIlliams' rule). THE SAME WEEKLY RUN IS THE REDISTRICTING TRIPWIRE: it re-reads the county-board page's Districts section letter by letter and fails if it stops matching the composition compiled into build_clay_boundaries.py. What it cannot trip is stated in the builder: the village-limits line splitting Clay City between districts A and B came from the Clerk's e-mail, and no page re-read can check a line the page never draws. No e-mail, party or term ships because the county publishes none. District C's letter was the one omission on the county's pages for weeks — Clerk Britton named Joe Goodman for it by e-mail (2026-08-24), and the county's own members page now states it too, which is the version that ships.

St. Clair's precinct -> polling place table — 149 precincts with a place and address, plus the county's one bare East St Louis feature carrying the Clerk's explanation that the city runs its own Board of Election Commissioners. THE SOURCE IS A CLERK-SENT DOCUMENT, NOT A PAGE: the county's published list groups precincts under combined human labels ('Belleville9,10, 12 & 16') that cannot be matched to single precincts without interpreting prose, which is what the st-clair-precinct-polling-places gap recorded since 31 Jul 2026. Asked for the same assignment one row per precinct, Sarah Hermsdorfer of the Clerk's Election Department sent 'St Clair County IL Polling Places.xlsx' on 2026-08-26; it is archived as a faithful CSV transcription under data/source/raw/ and joined by scripts/build_stclair_precinct_polling.py against the county's own precinct layer (prec_name2), so the shipped keys are exactly the strings the app looks up. THE SHEET'S HEADER IS A TRAP — its first column is titled POLLING PLACE and holds the PRECINCT name. One enumerated alias (the layer's 'Ofallon n' for the Clerk's 'O FALLON n'); the build fails on any other mismatch, any double-join, or any unmatched layer precinct besides East St Louis. FOUR ROWS CARRY THE CLERK'S ADVANCE NOTICE: Centreville 2, 5, 7 and 8 are set to move to the new Cahokia High School (805 Camp Jackson Rd) once the County Board votes on the change — the current assignment ships, the note rides those cards, and the file is stale for those four the day that vote passes. Operator step like Logan's and Carroll's: re-run when the Clerk sends an update.

The office and board of Boone County's five park and library taxing bodies, keyed by the same district name the two parcel-dissolve boundary files carry — the card joins the two, and scripts/build_boone_district_officials.py REFUSES TO WRITE unless the roster's keys are exactly the districts drawn, because a name drifting apart would empty a contact block silently while the polygon still drew. THE CLERK'S YEARBOOK OWNS THE OFFICE AND OWNS NO BOARD AT ALL, which is the correction this build made to its own gap record twice over. The booklet supplies the address, telephone, fax, website and agency head for all five; every BOARD comes from that body's own published page or document, because the booklet carries none for the three seated in Winnebago and is SUPERSEDED for the two seated in Boone — its Ida board predates that library's own 28 July 2026 officer election, and its Belvidere Park board predates a fifth commissioner the district itself lists. A VACANCY SHIPS ONLY WHERE THE BODY STATES ONE IN WORDS (Ida's list prints 'Trustee: Open'), never from seats-minus-rows: an earlier build derived Belvidere Park's that way and published '1 of 5 seats is vacant' about a district whose own page names five, because a markup quirk had hidden one. A roster short of the seats a body states now breaks the builder's floor instead. Rockford Park District is read from its plain /board page, NOT the ?format=json endpoint its robots.txt disallows. North Suburban's trustees come from a linked PDF, so the card cites the DOCUMENT and its Last-Modified date and the scraper warns if it predates the last April consolidated election. One address does not ship: Belvidere Park's Vice-President's row links one mailbox and displays another, and nothing settles which is current. Four Belvidere Park staff parse cleanly and are dropped on purpose — employees, not the governing body — and Ida's director ships as the library's own 'Library Director' with the library's own mindyl@ rather than the yearbook's 'Executive Director' and mistyped mindlyl@.

County board OFFICE ADDRESSES for the 33 districted counties whose own roster publishes none — the location row the fleet's card order asks for and the instance's largest card-order gap (county-board-office-addresses) was skipping on fifty of sixty-three cards. Each address is from ISBE's County Officers Book, published on the board chair's own row and emitted ONLY where a second courthouse office on the same county page prints the same street and city, so what ships is a shared public building and never anyone's home (the Madison/Peoria rule). THE SAME DOCUMENT'S CHAIR NAME COLUMN IS READ NOWHERE IN THIS APP and must stay that way — its disagreement rate with the counties' own rosters was 16 of the 56 counties then comparable (29%) when measured 2026-08-20, and 23 of 75 (30.7%) on a fresh rebuild 2026-09-06; it moves because the COMPARABLE SET grows as counties ship rosters, not because the document decays, so quote it with its date. The address column is a different column with a different failure mode — a chair turns over every cycle, a courthouse does not move — which is why it carries its own standing proof: build_county_board_offices.py re-runs the agreement test against every county that publishes its own board address (7 of 7 today) and refuses to write on any disagreement. THE REAL FLOOR ON THIS FILE IS MIN_OFFICES = 30 IN THAT BUILDER, not min_keys below: the top level holds exactly two keys, `note` and `offices`, so min_keys 2 asserts the file has a shape and nothing about how many counties are in it. A county that publishes its own address is excluded from this file, so its publication can never be overwritten; the card names the source and the document's date on the row.

history_page.intro: districtry Illinois began as a Chicago-only explorer and grew outward one county at a time — 91 of the state's 102 counties as of 26 August 2026. The counties that are missing are missing for reasons this project measured and wrote down, not for want of looking, and every one of them is on the record in the app's own data-gaps panel. This page is the deployment's record: what it ships, what it re-reads on a schedule, and the corrections its own machinery has caught.

entries.title: Clay, the ninety-first county
entries.body: Clay County's board districts ship, taking the map to 91 of Illinois's 102 counties. Its fourteen lettered districts were never the problem — the county publishes them, and seven are independently confirmed by certified 2026 primary returns — but the census draws one Clay City precinct where the county runs two districts through it, and nothing published said where that line falls. County Clerk Amy Britton answered in two sentences: District A is the village of Clay City, District B the unincorporated area around it. That is a corporate-limits line the census already draws, so the split was resolved block by block — 833 people inside the village, 333 outside, every block sorting cleanly to one side, and the two blocks that sit on the margin shipped with their measured precinct rather than absorbed quietly. Two of the districts sit further from equal population than this project's own ceiling normally allows; they ship only because the Clerk confirmed the map is current, and the measured figure is recorded rather than smoothed. Clay ships its board and not its precincts, because its two published surfaces disagree on how many precincts it has, and a precinct card would state more than is known.

entries.title: A county held back by its own numbers, and the letter that released it
entries.body: Wayne County's district composition had been corroborated twice over for weeks: the county's own board page states which precincts make up each of its seven districts, and its certified November 2024 General — 27 precinct-level results grouped by which board candidate each precinct actually voted on — partitions the same 27 precincts the same way, agreeing on six of seven exactly. The one difference is the county seat, where the board page omits two Fairfield precincts that the certified ballot shows voting in District 7, so the page is incomplete rather than the ballots wrong. None of that was the blocker. Composed against an ideal of 2,311 people, one district deviates by 32.4% — past the 30% ceiling this project enforces everywhere else, and both sources agreed on that district exactly, which is what made the number worth pausing over instead of dismissing as a mis-transcription. Clerk Elizabeth Woodrow was asked directly whether the plan had moved since it was drawn. Her reply: “Nothing has changed with this map for years.” The ceiling was raised for Wayne alone rather than widened for the fleet, and the measured deviation is on the record.

entries.title: Four counties in one day, and a lesson about labels
entries.body: Richland, Jackson, Douglas and Vermilion all join. Vermilion is the largest county the project has added and the one that teaches the most: it publishes three board-district layers, and the best-labelled one is obsolete. A service described as “Governmental and school districts” holds the 2011 plan, while the plan actually in force is an undocumented layer with a typo in its own name. Currency is a measurement, not a reading of a name — a plan drawn to a census balances on that census, and across 4,943 census blocks the layer that ships runs within 0.7% of equal population where the better-labelled one runs 15.1% out. The builder now refuses to write if that comparison ever reverses, in either direction. Jackson, the same day, is the first county in the fleet whose districts split precincts and are built anyway: its adopted map is a vector PDF whose districts are real polygon objects, so the shapes were read from the file rather than sampled from its pixels, and nothing traced ships — the map only ever chose between the two districts the county's own canvass had already named.

entries.title: A county is not blocked because its website is
entries.body: Knox County had been recorded as refusing every request. That was true of knoxcountyil.gov, and it was written down as though it described the county. Knox has four hosts: the website denies, a public GIS server answers and carries the county's twenty townships, the same site's document store has no block at all, and a fourth is simply dead. Knox joined as the 80th county — the first to join by closing an enclave rather than extending the frontier, filling a hole that seven already-served neighbours had left around it. Its districts come from the county's own adopted map, checked against certified returns and census population before shipping; a faster method that read the map's fill colours was tried first, produced a clean and confident answer, and was wrong, which is why that arithmetic check is now a gate in the builder rather than a comment in it. The frontier probe now sweeps GIS subdomains too, because the old host list could never have found the one host that mattered.

entries.title: Two counties that were never dark
entries.body: Gallatin's record said the county was dark on every route tried, and that its clerk's own mail domain did not resolve. Neither was true. The site answers normally and serves an incomplete certificate chain — the leaf without its intermediate — which every automated client reports as a hard failure and which no browser notices, so a misconfiguration had been recorded as an absence. Coles County had taught the pattern days earlier; sweeping all 27 frontier counties' clerk domains for the same shape found Gallatin and confirmed Vermilion, whose record had likewise said its site could not be reached. The fix supplies the missing intermediate and pins its fingerprint, rather than turning certificate verification off.

entries.title: Four websites that answer perfectly and serve nothing
entries.body: A sweep of all 406 municipal websites this app links found four that return a clean HTTP 200 and no content a reader wants: one is a domain-for-sale lander, one an entirely empty body, and two the default placeholder page that ships with an unconfigured web server. This is the one failure a status-code check cannot see — the link gate asks whether a URL answers, and all four answer flawlessly. The tell is content, and the cheap version of it is size: every one of the four came back under 1,200 bytes, against real municipal front pages that run to tens of thousands. None of them entered the roster by mistake — each is the website that municipality's own county publishes for it, so the counties are citing them too, and this project does not overwrite a county's published value on its own initiative. They are recorded as gaps instead.

entries.title: A clerk said there were no maps, and the county built anyway
entries.body: Clark County's Clerk answered the standing request with one sentence: the County Board is elected by districts, and no maps are available. That settles the board's form and refuses its geometry in the same breath. But Clark's districts are unions of whole precincts, so the county's own certified canvasses describe them completely, and the census voting districts — matching all 23 precinct names and summing to the county's exact population — supply the polygons. It is the first county in the fleet built entirely from election returns, with no map at any stage. Because a certified return names who won an election rather than who holds the seat today, every roster row names the election that seated the member instead of claiming a currency the returns cannot show.

entries.title: The first boundary this project ever bought
entries.body: Jo Daviess County's GIS office sells its data under a signed licence rather than publishing it. Its board-district shapefile ships displayed under the county's written permission — a purchased licence plus the IT/GIS Director's authorisation by e-mail — with the raw file retained offline rather than committed to this repository. It is the 63rd county, and the first whose boundary was paid for.

entries.title: The guard that measured the wrong thing
entries.body: Brown County's website switched on Cloudflare's e-mail obfuscation, so every published mailto: link became an encoded attribute instead. The scraper read mailto: only, and returned seven board members carrying zero e-mail addresses — while the guard that checks Brown seats seven passed happily. Seven rows in, seven rows out, guard satisfied, contact gone, on a tool whose whole purpose is telling residents how to reach their board. A count guard answers “did this break?” and cannot answer “does this still say what it said?”, so a retention gate now compares every roster field against the same file before the change and fails when a field stops being published — no threshold to configure, and a field is protected the moment it first ships. The obvious follow-up question was then measured rather than reassured about: all 25 other scrapers reading mailto: were fetched and checked, and none served the obfuscated form.

entries.title: A dead link nobody was checking
entries.body: Macon County's precinct card had been linking maconcountyil.gov for three days. That hostname has no DNS record at all — not a redirect, not a 404, no address associated with it. The county is at maconcounty.illinois.gov. Nothing in this repository checked the URLs the cards actually render: one gate covered the dataset endpoints the layers fetch and another covered layer counts, while the link a reader clicks was unguarded. A link gate now extracts its own surface from the app's authored pages and every roster file — around 1,200 URLs across some 540 hosts — so a new county is covered the day it ships, with nothing to remember to update. It separates links this project chose, which fail, from links carried through from a county's own published roster, which warn.

entries.title: Contiguity stops deciding which county comes next
entries.body: Until this day a county could only join if it touched the area already served, which meant the shape of the map was choosing the work rather than the data being available. That gate was retired: a county now joins whenever a county-keyed layer answers in it, wherever it sits. The served area is allowed to be disjoint, and has been four times since — each island rejoining as soon as a neighbouring county filled the gap, and the outline recomputed from the counties themselves every time rather than patched by hand. The honesty test it replaced is unchanged: a county is never joined just because some statewide layer happens to give a rich answer there.
